On 10 November 2026, OpenAI opened a door marketers have been asking for since AI search took off. Businesses in ChatGPT, now in beta, lets you claim your business profile, correct the details ChatGPT shows, add your products and see how often it mentions you. It won't make ChatGPT recommend you more. But it gives you control over your facts, and the first data from OpenAI itself on how you show up.
That's the short answer. Here's my launch-day read: what it is, how it compares to Google Business Profile, what it won't do, and the five things I'd do this week.
Businesses in ChatGPT is an OpenAI beta, launched on 10 November 2026, that lets verified owners claim and correct their business profile inside ChatGPT.
Claimed profiles get a blue check and aggregated insights, including mentions, views, website clicks and the topics people discuss when ChatGPT cites your site.
OpenAI says claiming a profile, or paying for ChatGPT Ads, does not change how often ChatGPT recommends a business.

What is Businesses in ChatGPT, in plain language?
Think of it as a front desk for your brand inside ChatGPT.
Until now, ChatGPT built its picture of your business from whatever it found on the web: your website, directories, reviews and news. If that picture was wrong, you had no direct way to fix it.

Business Hub, the dashboard behind it, changes that. If you own a business with a website, or you're authorised to represent one, you can claim its profile. OpenAI confirms the claim through a business phone number, email address, website domain or Shopify account. Once claimed, the profile shows a blue check. (OpenAI's announcement)

From there you can update your name, category, address or service area, hours, contact details and products or services. Retailers can upload product feeds with pricing and availability, and Shopify merchants can connect their store directly.

There's a second layer called Business Agents. It's a labelled chat, built on your information, that a customer can open from your profile to ask questions. For now, it's only for eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the US.
ChatGPT used to only talk about your business. Now you get to talk back.

That's the comparison every marketer will make, and it's mostly fair.

The big difference is the last row. On Google, a well-kept profile is part of how you win local search. On ChatGPT, OpenAI is clear that recommendations stay independent.
Does claiming your business help you rank in ChatGPT?

No. OpenAI says claiming does not guarantee higher placement or sales. Paying for ChatGPT Ads doesn't change how often ChatGPT recommends a business either, and sponsored placements are labelled separately from answers (Reuters, 10 November 2026).
First, accuracy. When ChatGPT gets your hours, prices or services wrong, you now have a place to correct them.

Second, measurement. For the first time, mentions and clicks come straight from OpenAI, not from a third-party tracker running sample prompts. Here's the thing: that's the part I'm most interested in.
Claiming won't win you the recommendation. Your website, your reviews and what others say about you still do that.

That's why the work on your own site, like clear schema markup and consistent sameAs links, still matters more than any profile. The same habits that help you show up in Google's AI Overviews apply here.
Check what ChatGPT says today. Ask it about your business by name, by category and by location. Save the answers.

Claim the profile. Start at chatgpt.com/business-hub. If you manage accounts for clients, the owner should claim it or authorise you to. OpenAI Enterprise customers and advertisers go through their OpenAI representative.
Fix the facts, then match them everywhere. Your hours, address and services should read the same in ChatGPT, on your website, on your Google Business Profile and in your schema.
Add your products. Retailers should upload a product feed or connect Shopify, so prices and availability stay current.
Set a baseline. When your first mentions and clicks appear, note them, and add ChatGPT to your monthly report next to Google.
It's a beta, and it shows.
Insights only appear once activity passes thresholds OpenAI hasn't disclosed, so smaller businesses may see nothing for a while.
The blue check means the profile is claimed, not that every detail is checked. OpenAI says profiles can include information from other sources.
Not every business can claim. Eligibility depends on industry, location and verification checks.
Business Agents are US-only for now. In the UAE you can claim a profile, but you can't launch an agent yet.
For healthcare brands, I'd be careful. Keep the profile to plain facts like specialities, locations and hours, and let your compliance team see it before it goes live.

Before you claim anything, ask ChatGPT five questions a customer would ask, such as "best dermatology clinic in Dubai" or "what are [your brand]'s opening hours?". Screenshot the answers and date them. In three months, you'll have a real before and after, not a guess.

Businesses in ChatGPT is an OpenAI beta, launched on 10 November 2026, that lets businesses claim a profile inside ChatGPT. Through a dashboard called Business Hub, verified owners can update their details, add products and see aggregated insights on mentions, views and website clicks. Eligible US businesses can also build a Business Agent that answers customer questions.
How do I claim my business in ChatGPT?

Go to chatgpt.com/business-hub and start a claim. You need to own the business or be authorised to represent it, and the business needs a website. OpenAI confirms the claim through a business phone number, email address, website domain or Shopify account. Enterprise customers and advertisers claim through their OpenAI representative instead.
Does claiming my business improve my ranking in ChatGPT?

No. OpenAI says claiming a profile does not guarantee higher placement or sales, and that ChatGPT continues to make independent recommendations. Paying for ChatGPT Ads doesn't change how often it recommends a business either. Claiming helps you keep your information accurate and gives you data on how often ChatGPT mentions you.
Is Businesses in ChatGPT available in the UAE?

Eligible businesses can claim a profile wherever ChatGPT is available, which includes the UAE. Business Agents, the branded chats customers open from a profile, are currently limited to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the United States. OpenAI says it plans to expand over time but hasn't shared dates.
What insights does Business Hub show?

Business Hub shows aggregated insights: how often ChatGPT mentions your business, profile views, clicks to your website and discovery topics, which are common themes in conversations that cite your site. The data only appears once activity passes OpenAI's thresholds. OpenAI says it does not share users' conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses.
